narrative.overview:
The dashboard reads like a Swiss station's information system: a dark
departure board, the rail and the strip across the top, sits over a
paper-white working ground where the projects are listed like a timetable. One glance answers what is on time, what is late,
what is running, and what needs the maintainer, and the board is the only
place the interface raises its voice.

It is an Operate surface. Scanning dozens of projects quickly matters more
than expression, so the brand lives in precise details: the station clock's
red second disc stepping on the shared tick, condensed tabular figures for
every time and count, hairline rules instead of boxes, and status written as a
glyph and a word, never as colour alone. The board stays dark in both themes
(a shade deeper at night); the theme switch changes the ground beneath it.
keyCharacteristics: A dark board (rail and departures strip) over a paper or night ground.
Signal red is reserved for failures and lateness; everything that only waits for a decision is amber.
One grotesk with a width axis; numbers condense, words do not.
Hairline-ruled rows, small radii, no shadows on content.
Every view is built from the backend's own schemas, so the system is the renderer's vocabulary, not a set of one-off screens.

rules.name: The Red Reservation Rule
rules.body: Red means failed or late, nothing else. A parked conflict, an unread notification, or drift from forge is amber.

rules.name: The Board Rule
rules.body: Red and amber text on the board always use the board variants; the working-ground reds are for the paper.

rules.name: The Condensed Digits Rule
rules.body: `.figures` applies only to the number in "20 min ago"; the unit stays at normal width so it never reads as one word.

rules.name: The Mono Id Rule
rules.body: A project's id, a branch, a hash, or a path is always set in the code face, so it can be read and copied exactly.

rules.name: The Flat Ground Rule
rules.body: Depth is drawn with rules and fills, not shadows: a 1px rule separates rows and cards, the heavier rule-strong underlines section headings and table heads, and a selected card gets a 1px info ring. Cards, tables, and the board carry no shadow. Form controls keep the component library's hairline `shadow-xs`; popovers and menus use `shadow-md`, and dialogs and sheets `shadow-lg`, because they genuinely sit above the page.

dos: **Do** write every status as a glyph and a word.
**Do** keep red for failed and late; use amber for anything waiting.
**Do** set times and counts in condensed tabular figures, and only those.
**Do** separate with hairline rules and alignment rather than boxes.
**Do** add a field to the backend model with a `slot` or `columns` hint instead of hand-placing it in a component.
donts: **Don't** put a chart in every tile or a sparkline on a flat series.
**Don't** use signal red for drift, parked work, or unread counts.
**Don't** add shadows to cards or tables.
**Don't** introduce a second display face or decorative imagery; this build is code-led and ships no rasters.
**Don't** let a layout scroll sideways on a phone; give grids a shrinkable base column.
